questions.q: When two or more related quantities change by the same factor, what do we call the relationship between them?
questions.a: a proportional relationship

questions.q: Which pair of ratios is proportional?
(a) Find the two cross products for the ratios 6 : 11 and 18 : 33. (b) Are the two ratios proportional? Write your answer using the :: notation if they are.
questions.a: (a) 6 x 33 = 198 and 11 x 18 = 198. (b) The cross products are equal, so the ratios are proportional: 6 : 11 :: 18 : 33.
s: (b) Concludes they are proportional and writes 6 : 11 :: 18 : 33

questions.q: True or false: The ratios 2 : 3 and 4 : 5 are proportional, because in both ratios the second term is 1 more than the first. Give the reason.
questions.a: False. The cross products are 2 x 5 = 10 and 3 x 4 = 12, which are not equal. Having the same difference between the terms does not make two ratios proportional; the terms must change by the same factor.
s: Gives the reason: cross products 10 and 12 are unequal; same difference is not the same factor

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The ratios 3 : 4 and 6 : 7 are proportional.
Reason (R): Two ratios a : b and c : d are proportional when a x d = b x c.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: Rina mixes 4 spoons of sugar with 6 glasses of water. Gopi mixes 6 spoons of sugar with 12 glasses of water. They pour both lemonades into one big jug. Which of these has the same sugar : water ratio as the lemonade in the jug?
questions.a: 15 spoons of sugar for 27 glasses of water
o: 15 spoons of sugar for 27 glasses of water
10 spoons of sugar for 15 glasses of water
12 spoons of sugar for 24 glasses of water
9 spoons of sugar for 15 glasses of water

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. If a : b :: c : d, then a : c :: b : d is also true.
II. The ratios 2.5 : 4 and 5 : 8 are proportional.
III. If 3 : 5 :: 12 : x, then x = 15.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and II only

questions.q: Kavya says, 'The ratios 12 : 16 and 15 : 20 are proportional, but if I swap the middle numbers to get 12 : 15 and 16 : 20, those two ratios are not proportional.' Test both pairs by cross multiplication and say whether Kavya is right.
questions.a: First pair: 12 x 20 = 240 and 16 x 15 = 240, so 12 : 16 :: 15 : 20. Second pair: 12 x 20 = 240 and 15 x 16 = 240, so 12 : 15 :: 16 : 20 as well. Kavya is only partly right: the first part of her claim is correct, but the second pair is also proportional, because the cross products use the same four numbers.
s: Verdict: partly right; the second pair is also proportional because the same products appear

questions.q:
Three dairies sell the same curd. Dairy P sells 400 g for Rs 32, Dairy Q sells 1,000 g for Rs 80 and Dairy R sells 750 g for Rs 63. Each dairy sells only whole packs of that size.
(a) Use cross multiplication to test whether P's weight : price ratio is proportional to Q's.
(b) Use cross multiplication to test whether P's weight : price ratio is proportional to R's.
(c) Find the price of 100 g of curd at each dairy, and name the dairy with the dearer rate.
(d) A hostel needs at least 3 kg of curd and must buy it all from one dairy. How many packs would it buy at each dairy, and what would they cost?
(e) Which dairy should the hostel choose? Explain why the dairy with the dearer rate is not the most costly choice here.
questions.a: (a) 400 x 80 = 32,000 and 32 x 1,000 = 32,000, so P and Q are proportional. (b) 400 x 63 = 25,200 and 32 x 750 = 24,000, so P and R are not proportional. (c) P: Rs 8, Q: Rs 8, R: Rs 8.40 per 100 g, so Dairy R has the dearer rate. (d) P: 3,000 / 400 = 7.5, so 8 packs (3.2 kg) costing 8 x 32 = Rs 256. Q: 3 packs (3 kg) costing 3 x 80 = Rs 240. R: 3,000 / 750 = 4 packs (3 kg) costing 4 x 63 = Rs 252. (e) Dairy Q, at Rs 240. R has the dearer rate but costs Rs 252, less than P's Rs 256, because P's 400 g packs force the hostel to buy 200 g more than it needs.
s: (a) Cross products 32,000 and 32,000; P and Q proportional
(b) Cross products 25,200 and 24,000; P and R not proportional
(c) Rs 8, Rs 8 and Rs 8.40 per 100 g; R is dearer
(d) P: 8 packs, Rs 256; Q: 3 packs, Rs 240; R: 4 packs, Rs 252
(e) Chooses Q; explains P costs more than R because of the extra 200 g

questions.q:
A paint shop in Coimbatore mixes a 'sky blue' shade using white paint and blue paint in the ratio white : blue = 7 : 2. On Monday three orders were mixed by a new helper:
Order 1: 14 litres of white and 4 litres of blue.
Order 2: 21 litres of white and 5 litres of blue.
Order 3: 3.5 litres of white and 1 litre of blue.
The owner checks each order before it goes out.
(a) Find the two cross products that test Order 1 against 7 : 2.
(b) Is Order 2 proportional to 7 : 2? Show the check.
(c) Is Order 3 proportional to 7 : 2? Show the check.
(d) The owner will fix the wrong order by adding blue paint only. How much more blue paint must be added?
questions.a: (a) 14 x 2 = 28 and 4 x 7 = 28, so Order 1 is proportional. (b) 21 x 2 = 42 and 5 x 7 = 35, which are not equal, so Order 2 is not proportional. (c) 3.5 x 2 = 7 and 1 x 7 = 7, so Order 3 is proportional. (d) For 21 litres of white, blue should be 21 x 2 / 7 = 6 litres, so 6 - 5 = 1 more litre of blue is needed.
s: (b) Cross products 42 and 35; Order 2 not proportional
(d) Blue needed is 6 litres, so 1 litre more is added

questions.q: A map has the Representative Fraction (RF) 1 : 50,00,000. Which statement reads this RF correctly?
questions.a: 1 cm on the map stands for 50,00,000 cm on the ground.
o: 1 cm on the map stands for 50,00,000 cm on the ground.
1 cm on the map stands for 50,00,000 km on the ground.
1 cm on the ground stands for 50,00,000 cm on the map.
50,00,000 cm on the map stands for 1 cm on the ground.

questions.q: A map has RF 1 : 35,00,000, so 1 cm on it stands for 35,00,000 cm on the ground. How many kilometres is 35,00,000 cm?
questions.a: 35 km

questions.q: A map has RF 1 : 80,00,000. (a) How many kilometres on the ground does 1 cm on this map stand for? (b) Two cities are 4.5 cm apart on this map. Find the geographical distance between them.
questions.a: (a) 80,00,000 cm = 80 km, so 1 cm stands for 80 km. (b) 4.5 x 80 = 360 km.

questions.q:
A state map has RF 1 : 12,00,000.
(a) How many kilometres does 1 cm on the map stand for?
(b) Two towns are 7 cm apart on the map. Find their geographical distance.
(c) Two other towns are 90 km apart on the ground. How far apart are they on the map?

Assertion (A): On a map with RF 1 : 10,00,000, a distance of 1 cm stands for 10 km on the ground.
Reason (R): The RF on a map usually has 1 as its first term and a very large number as its second term.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Two hill towns are 63 km apart (geographical distance). A student wants to mark them on a map drawn with RF 1 : 18,00,000. How far apart should she mark them?
questions.a: 3.5 cm

questions.q: True or false: Two towns are 10 cm apart in a straight line on a map with RF 1 : 4,00,000, so a bus going from one town to the other by road must travel exactly 40 km. Give the reason.
questions.a: False. 10 x 4,00,000 cm = 40,00,000 cm = 40 km is the geographical (straight-line) distance between the towns. The RF gives geographical distance, not road distance, and a road usually does not run in a straight line, so the bus may travel a different, longer distance.
s: Gives the reason: 40 km is the geographical distance from the RF, not the road distance

questions.q:
A forest department's map of a wildlife sanctuary has RF 1 : 25,000.
(a) How many metres on the ground does 1 cm on this map stand for?
(b) A straight path between two watch-towers measures 9.6 cm on the map. Find its geographical length in kilometres.
(c) The department plans a straight fire-line 4 km long. How long should it be drawn on the map?

Map A of a district has its scale written as '1 cm stands for 5 km'. Map B of the same district has RF 1 : 2,50,000.
(a) Write the scale of Map A as an RF in the form 1 : k.
(b) On Map A, two bus stands are 7.4 cm apart. Find their geographical distance.
(c) How far apart are the same two bus stands on Map B?
(d) A lake is 1.25 km wide. How wide does it appear on Map A and on Map B?
(e) A planner wants the lake's shape to show as clearly as possible. Which map should she use, and why?
questions.a: (a) 5 km = 5,00,000 cm, so Map A has RF 1 : 5,00,000. (b) 7.4 x 5 = 37 km. (c) 37 km = 37,00,000 cm, and 37,00,000 / 2,50,000 = 14.8 cm. (d) 1.25 km = 1,25,000 cm. Map A: 1,25,000 / 5,00,000 = 0.25 cm. Map B: 1,25,000 / 2,50,000 = 0.5 cm. (e) Map B, because its RF has the smaller second term, so every length on it is drawn twice as long as on Map A and the lake appears twice as wide.
s: (c) Distance on Map B is 14.8 cm
(d) Lake width 0.25 cm on Map A and 0.5 cm on Map B
(e) Chooses Map B because lengths there are twice as long

questions.q:
Leela lives in the village of Kherwa. Her school atlas has a district map with RF 1 : 5,00,000. She measures the straight-line distances on the map from Kherwa to three places the class may visit on a one-day trip: the market town is 3.4 cm away, the district headquarters is 9 cm away and the dam is 5.6 cm away. The school allows a trip only to places within 40 km of the village (geographical distance).
(a) How many kilometres does 1 cm on this map stand for?
(b) Find the geographical distance from Kherwa to the market town.
(c) Find the geographical distance from Kherwa to the district headquarters.
(d) Which of the three places can the class visit under the school's rule?
questions.a: (a) 5,00,000 cm = 5 km. (b) 3.4 x 5 = 17 km. (c) 9 x 5 = 45 km. (d) The dam is 5.6 x 5 = 28 km away. The market town (17 km) and the dam (28 km) are within 40 km; the district headquarters (45 km) is not, so the class can visit the market town and the dam.
s: (d) Finds the dam at 28 km and chooses the market town and the dam

questions.q: A vegetable pulao uses rice : water : chopped vegetables = 2 : 4 : 3 (in cups). How many cups of vegetables go with 6 cups of rice, keeping the same ratio?
questions.a: 9 cups

questions.q: Which ratio is proportional to 3 : 6 : 9?

A garden fertiliser is mixed as nitrogen granules : phosphate : potash = 4 : 2 : 1 (in spoons). Manju has 10 spoons of phosphate and wants the same mix. (a) By what factor must every term be multiplied? (b) How many spoons of nitrogen granules and of potash does she need?
questions.a: (a) Phosphate goes from 2 to 10, so the factor is 10 / 2 = 5. (b) Nitrogen granules = 4 x 5 = 20 spoons and potash = 1 x 5 = 5 spoons.
s: (b) Finds 20 spoons of nitrogen granules and 5 spoons of potash

questions.q:
A sweet shop makes chikki with jaggery : peanuts : sesame seeds : cashews = 6 : 4 : 2 : 1 (in cups). Today it has exactly 3 cups of sesame seeds and wants to use all of them.
(a) Find the factor by which every term must be multiplied.
(b) How many cups of jaggery are needed?
(c) How many cups of peanuts are needed?
(d) How many cups of cashews are needed?
(e) What is the total number of cups of all four ingredients?
questions.a: (a) Sesame goes from 2 to 3, so the factor is 3 / 2 = 1.5. (b) Jaggery = 6 x 1.5 = 9 cups. (c) Peanuts = 4 x 1.5 = 6 cups. (d) Cashews = 1 x 1.5 = 1.5 cups. (e) Total = 9 + 6 + 3 + 1.5 = 19.5 cups.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): 2 : 3 : 5 :: 4 : 6 : 10.
Reason (R): Each term of 4 : 6 : 10 is 2 more than the matching term of 2 : 3 : 5.
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
Match each ratio in Column I with the ratio in Column II that is proportional to it.
Column I: I. 2 : 3 : 4  II. 4 : 2 : 1  III. 2 : 2.5 : 4  IV. 5 : 2 : 2
Column II: A. 8 : 4 : 2  B. 6 : 7.5 : 12  C. 7.5 : 3 : 3  D. 1 : 1.5 : 2
questions.a: I-D, II-A, III-B, IV-C

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. If 4 : 6 : 9 :: 6 : p : q, then p = 9 and q = 13.5.
II. Doubling the first two terms of 5 : 3 : 2 and keeping the third gives 10 : 6 : 2, which is proportional to 5 : 3 : 2.
III. 6 : 9 : 3 : 12 :: 4 : 6 : 2 : 8.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and III only

questions.q: Sanjay makes a plant spray with neem oil : soap solution : water = 1 : 2 : 40 (in spoons). He has 5 spoons of soap solution and says, 'My soap solution is 3 spoons more than in the ratio, so I add 3 spoons to each of the others: 4 spoons of neem oil and 43 spoons of water.' Check his amounts and say whether he is right.
questions.a: The soap solution goes from 2 to 5, so every term must be multiplied by 5 / 2 = 2.5. Neem oil = 1 x 2.5 = 2.5 spoons, not 4. Water = 40 x 2.5 = 100 spoons, not 43. Sanjay is wrong: he added 3 to every term instead of multiplying every term by the same factor.
s: Finds the scale factor 2.5 from the soap solution
Finds neem oil should be 2.5 spoons, not 4
Finds water should be 100 spoons, not 43; he added instead of multiplying, so he is wrong

questions.q:
A dairy farmer meant to make 20 kg of cattle feed with maize : wheat bran : oil cake = 5 : 3 : 2, but by mistake mixed the 20 kg in the ratio 5 : 2 : 3. He cannot take anything out of the feed; he can only add more maize, bran or oil cake.
(a) How many kg of maize, bran and oil cake are in his feed now?
(b) Which ingredient needs nothing added, and what factor does it fix for the ratio 5 : 3 : 2?
(c) How much maize and how much bran must he add to reach 5 : 3 : 2 with the least amount added?
(d) Find the new total weight and check that the new amounts are in the ratio 5 : 3 : 2.
questions.a: (a) 20 / (5 + 2 + 3) = 2 kg per part, so maize 10 kg, bran 4 kg, oil cake 6 kg. (b) Nothing can be removed, so every amount must be at least its share: maize needs a factor of at least 10 / 5 = 2, bran 4 / 3 (about 1.33) and oil cake 6 / 2 = 3. The largest, 3, is the least factor that works, so oil cake stays at 6 kg and needs nothing added; the factor is 3. (c) Maize should be 5 x 3 = 15 kg, so add 5 kg of maize. Bran should be 3 x 3 = 9 kg, so add 5 kg of bran. (d) New total = 15 + 9 + 6 = 30 kg, and 15 : 9 : 6 = 5 : 3 : 2 (dividing every term by 3).
s: (a) Finds maize 10 kg, bran 4 kg, oil cake 6 kg
(b) Names oil cake (nothing added) and finds the factor 3
(c) Adds 5 kg of maize and 5 kg of bran

questions.q:
A bakery in Kochi makes plum cake batter from a standard batch of 800 g of flour, 600 g of sugar, 400 g of butter and 200 g of dry fruit. For a Christmas order, the baker wants to use one whole 1.5 kg block of butter and keep the batter tasting exactly the same, so every ingredient must stay in the same ratio as the standard batch.
(a) Write flour : sugar : butter : dry fruit in its simplest form.
(b) If all 1.5 kg of butter is used, how much flour, sugar and dry fruit are needed?
(c) Find the total weight of this batter.
(d) The store has only 1.8 kg of sugar. Can the baker use the whole block of butter? If not, what is the most butter he can use?
questions.a: (a) Dividing every term by 200 gives 4 : 3 : 2 : 1. (b) Butter is 2 parts = 1.5 kg, so 1 part = 0.75 kg: flour = 3 kg, sugar = 2.25 kg, dry fruit = 0.75 kg. (c) 3 + 2.25 + 1.5 + 0.75 = 7.5 kg. (d) No: the batch needs 2.25 kg of sugar but only 1.8 kg is there. Using all the sugar, 3 parts = 1.8 kg, so 1 part = 0.6 kg and butter = 2 x 0.6 = 1.2 kg at most.
s: (b) Flour 3 kg, sugar 2.25 kg, dry fruit 0.75 kg
(d) Not enough sugar; the most butter is 1.2 kg

questions.q: 84 is divided into two parts in the ratio 3 : 4. What is the larger part?
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 8. What is the largest angle?
questions.a: 96 degrees

questions.q: Rs 2,400 is shared between two sisters in the ratio 5 : 3. (a) Find each sister's share. (b) How much more does the elder sister, who gets the larger share, receive?
questions.a: (a) Sum of terms = 8, and 2,400 / 8 = 300. Shares: 5 x 300 = Rs 1,500 and 3 x 300 = Rs 900. (b) 1,500 - 900 = Rs 600 more.
s: (a) Finds the shares Rs 1,500 and Rs 900

questions.q:
A community kitchen divides 1,800 g of flour among three cooks in the ratio 1 : 2.5 : 1.5.
(a) Find the sum of the terms of the ratio.
(b) Find the value of one part.
(c) Find how many grams of flour each cook gets.
True or false: A triangle can have its angles in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2, and its largest angle is then 90 degrees. Give the reason.
questions.a: True. The angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. 180 / (1 + 1 + 2) = 45, so the angles are 45, 45 and 90 degrees, which add to 180 degrees.
s: Gives the reason: 180 / 4 = 45, so the angles are 45, 45 and 90 degrees

questions.q:
Assertion (A): No triangle can be drawn with its sides in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5.
Reason (R): In any triangle, the sum of the lengths of any two sides is greater than the third side.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A school drama sold 64 tickets, only Rs 50 tickets and Rs 20 tickets. The number of Rs 50 tickets to the number of Rs 20 tickets is 3 : 5. How much money did the ticket sales bring in?

In a school cricket match, the runs scored by Anil, Bharat and Chetan were in the ratio 4 : 5 : 7. Anil scored 36 runs.
(a) Find the number of runs in one part of the ratio.
(b) Find the runs scored by Bharat and by Chetan.
(c) Find the total runs scored by the three batters.
questions.a: (a) Anil's 36 runs are 4 parts, so one part = 36 / 4 = 9 runs. (b) Bharat: 5 x 9 = 45 runs; Chetan: 7 x 9 = 63 runs. (c) Total = 36 + 45 + 63 = 144 runs (or 16 parts x 9 = 144).

questions.q:
A craft club bends pieces of wire into triangle frames, cutting each wire into three sides in a chosen ratio, with no wire left over.
(a) Which one of the ratios 3 : 5 : 6, 1 : 3 : 4 and 2 : 5 : 8 can give a triangle? Give the reason for each.
(b) The club uses the ratio from (a). A 70 cm wire is cut in this ratio. Find the three side lengths.
(c) Another frame in the same ratio must have its longest side 12 cm. How long a wire is needed?
(d) A member wants a frame in this ratio from a 50 cm wire with every side a whole number of cm. Is this possible? Give the reason.
(e) What is the longest wire, up to 50 cm, that can be cut in this ratio with every side a whole number of cm? Give its sides.
questions.a: (a) Only 3 : 5 : 6, since 3 + 5 = 8 > 6 (and the other sums are larger). For 1 : 3 : 4, 1 + 3 = 4 is not greater than 4; for 2 : 5 : 8, 2 + 5 = 7 is less than 8. (b) Sum of terms = 14, one part = 70 / 14 = 5 cm, so the sides are 15 cm, 25 cm and 30 cm. (c) The longest side is 6 parts, so one part = 12 / 6 = 2 cm; the wire is 14 x 2 = 28 cm (sides 6, 10 and 12 cm). (d) No. One part would be 50 / 14 = 3.57... cm, which is not a whole number, so the sides would not be whole numbers of cm. (e) The wire length must be a multiple of 14; the largest up to 50 is 42 cm, giving one part = 3 cm and sides 9 cm, 15 cm and 18 cm.
s: (a) Only 3 : 5 : 6, with the side-sum check for each ratio
(d) Not possible: 50 / 14 is not a whole number
(e) 42 cm wire with sides 9, 15 and 18 cm

questions.q:
Three neighbours in a village near Nashik share one borewell. They agreed to pay its monthly electricity bill in the ratio of the number of hours each one pumps water. In June the bill was Rs 3,600. Ganesh pumped for 30 hours, Lata for 45 hours and Imran for 25 hours. Lata now suggests that the bill should simply be split equally, Rs 1,200 each, because all three own the well equally.
(a) Write the ratio of their pumping hours in its simplest form.
(b) Find Ganesh's share of the bill under the agreed method.
(c) Find Lata's and Imran's shares under the agreed method.
(d) Who gains and who loses, and by how much, if Lata's equal split is used? Is the equal split fair for a bill that depends on use? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 30 : 45 : 25 = 6 : 9 : 5 (dividing by 5). (b) Sum of terms = 20, one part = 3,600 / 20 = Rs 180, so Ganesh pays 6 x 180 = Rs 1,080. (c) Lata pays 9 x 180 = Rs 1,620 and Imran pays 5 x 180 = Rs 900. (d) With Rs 1,200 each, Lata pays Rs 420 less, Ganesh pays Rs 120 more and Imran pays Rs 300 more. Equal ownership supports an equal split for costs of the well itself, but the electricity bill grows with the hours of pumping, so the agreed ratio is fairer: under the equal split Ganesh and Imran would pay for part of the electricity Lata used.
s: (d) Lata saves Rs 420, Ganesh pays Rs 120 more, Imran Rs 300 more; judges the usage-based ratio fairer with a reason

questions.q: In a pie chart, one category makes up 25% of the data. What is the angle of its sector?
questions.a: 90 degrees

questions.q: A sector of a pie chart has an angle of 120 degrees. What fraction of the whole data does it show?

In a class of 30 students, 12 chose kho-kho as their favourite game. (a) What fraction of the class chose kho-kho? Give it in simplest form. (b) Find the angle of the kho-kho sector in a pie chart of the class's choices.

72 students voted for their favourite fruit. Column I gives the votes for four of the fruits; the remaining 12 votes went to other fruits. Match the number of votes in Column I with the pie-chart sector angle in Column II.
Column I: I. 18 votes  II. 24 votes  III. 6 votes  IV. 12 votes
Column II: A. 60 degrees  B. 120 degrees  C. 90 degrees  D. 30 degrees
questions.a: I-C, II-B, III-D, IV-A

questions.q:
The 40 students of Class 8B each joined exactly one school club. The Science club has 10 members, the Art club 14, the Music club 12 and the Eco club 4. The class teacher asks the students to draw a pie chart of the club choices for the notice board, with one sector for each club.
(a) What angle of the circle stands for one student?
(b) Find the angle of the Science club sector.
(c) Find the angles of the Art club and Music club sectors.
(d) The teacher says the Art club sector will be more than one-third of the circle. Is she right? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) 360 / 40 = 9 degrees. (b) 10 x 9 = 90 degrees. (c) Art: 14 x 9 = 126 degrees; Music: 12 x 9 = 108 degrees. (d) Yes. One-third of the circle is 120 degrees and the Art sector is 126 degrees, which is more. (The Eco sector is 36 degrees, and 90 + 126 + 108 + 36 = 360 degrees.)
s: (d) Yes, because 126 degrees is more than 120 degrees

questions.q: A pie chart shows how 1,080 voters in a ward reached the polling booth. The 'walked' sector has an angle of 140 degrees. How many voters walked to the booth?

Consider the following statements about pie charts.
I. A category that is 35% of the data gets a sector of 135 degrees.
II. If the data is in the ratio 4 : 3 : 2, the sectors are 160, 120 and 80 degrees.
III. Data in the ratio 10 : 20 : 30 gives the same sector angles as data in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: II and III only

questions.q:
A pie chart shows how a school spent its sports grant of Rs 1,50,000 for the year: equipment 150 degrees, coaching 120 degrees, travel 60 degrees and refreshments 30 degrees.
(a) Write the ratio equipment : coaching : travel : refreshments in its simplest form.
(b) How much money was spent on coaching?
(c) What fraction of the grant went on refreshments, and how much money is that?

A town library recorded the 480 books borrowed in one week: story books 180, science books 72, history books 48 and comics 180.
(a) Write the ratio story : science : history : comics in its simplest form, using the HCF.
(b) Find the pie-chart angle for each kind of book.
(c) Check that your four angles make a full circle.
(d) The librarian wants to merge two kinds of book into one 'other' sector that is exactly a right angle. Which two kinds must she merge? Show that no other pair works.
(e) The library will buy new books in the same ratio as the borrowing. If it buys 24 history books, how many story, science and comic books should it buy?
questions.a: (a) The HCF of 180, 72, 48 and 180 is 12, so the ratio is 15 : 6 : 4 : 15 (sum 40). (b) One part = 360 / 40 = 9 degrees: story 135, science 54, history 36 and comics 135 degrees. (c) 135 + 54 + 36 + 135 = 360 degrees. (d) Science and history: 54 + 36 = 90 degrees. Every other pair includes a 135 degrees sector (story or comics), so its sum is at least 135 + 36 = 171 degrees, more than 90 degrees. (e) 24 history books are 4 parts, so one part = 6 books: story 15 x 6 = 90, science 6 x 6 = 36 and comics 15 x 6 = 90 books.
s: (c) Shows the angles add to 360 degrees
(d) Science and history (90 degrees); every other pair is 171 degrees or more

questions.q: True or false: In a pie chart, if one category has twice as many votes as another, its sector angle is also twice as large. Give the reason.
questions.a: True. Each sector angle is (frequency / total) x 360 degrees, so the angle is proportional to the frequency. Twice the frequency gives twice the angle.
s: Gives the reason: the angle is (frequency / total) x 360 degrees, so it is proportional to the frequency

questions.q: Which pair of quantities is in inverse proportion?
questions.a: The number of buses hired for a fixed group of students, and the number of students in each bus
o: The number of buses hired for a fixed group of students, and the number of students in each bus
The number of bus tickets bought at a fixed price, and the total cost of the tickets
The litres of milk bought at a fixed rate, and the money paid for the milk
The hours a fan runs at one speed, and the electricity the fan uses

questions.q: 6 metres of cloth cost Rs 540. At the same rate per metre, how much do 10 metres of the cloth cost?
questions.a: Rs 900

questions.q: 8 identical machines stitch an order of school uniforms in 9 days. (a) Are the number of machines and the number of days in direct or inverse proportion? (b) How many days will 12 such machines take for the same order?
questions.a: (a) Inverse proportion: more machines take fewer days for the same order. (b) 8 x 9 = 12 x y, so y = 72 / 12 = 6 days.
s: (a) Says inverse proportion, with the reason more machines need fewer days
(b) Uses 8 x 9 = 12 x y to get 6 days

questions.q:
A sweet shop packs a festival order of laddoos into boxes, with the same number of laddoos in every box and no laddoo left over. With 24 laddoos in a box, it needs 60 boxes.
(a) Are the number of laddoos in a box and the number of boxes in direct or inverse proportion? Give the reason.
(b) How many boxes are needed if each box holds 36 laddoos?
(c) How many laddoos go in each box if 45 boxes are used?
(d) The shop has only 30 boxes. What is the least number of laddoos each box must hold so that the whole order fits?
questions.a: (a) Inverse proportion: the total 24 x 60 = 1,440 laddoos is fixed, so if each box holds more, fewer boxes are needed, and the product stays 1,440. (b) 24 x 60 = 36 x n, so n = 1,440 / 36 = 40 boxes. (c) 1,440 / 45 = 32 laddoos in each box. (d) 1,440 / 30 = 48 laddoos in each box.
s: (a) Inverse proportion because the product 1,440 stays fixed
(d) At least 48 laddoos in each box

questions.q:
Assertion (A): 1,000 kg of rice fills 40 sacks of 25 kg each, so it fills 50 sacks of 20 kg each.
Reason (R): For a fixed amount of rice, the number of sacks and the weight in each sack are inversely proportional.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: 12 friends hire a bus for a school trip and share the hire charge equally, Rs 450 each. Then 4 more friends join, and the bus company adds Rs 600 to the charge for the extra seats. The new charge is shared equally by all 16. How much does each friend now pay?
questions.a: Rs 375

questions.q:
Ravi can wash a pile of dishes in 30 minutes. His sister can wash the same pile in 20 minutes.
(a) What part of the pile does each of them wash in 1 minute?
(b) What part of the pile do they wash together in 1 minute?
(c) How long will they take to wash the pile together?
questions.a: (a) Ravi washes 1/30 and his sister 1/20 of the pile in 1 minute. (b) 1/30 + 1/20 = 2/60 + 3/60 = 5/60 = 1/12 of the pile. (c) They wash 1/12 of the pile each minute, so the whole pile takes 12 minutes.
s: (a) Rates 1/30 and 1/20 of the pile per minute
(b) Combined rate 1/12 of the pile per minute

questions.q:
Match each table of x and y values in Column I with its description in Column II.
Column I:
I. x: 2, 4, 8 and y: 12, 6, 3
II. x: 2, 4, 8 and y: 6, 12, 24
III. x: 2, 4, 8 and y: 5, 7, 11
IV. x: 3, 6, 9 and y: 12, 6, 4
Column II:
A. Direct proportion; each y is 3 times its x
B. Inverse proportion; each product xy is 24
C. Inverse proportion; each product xy is 36
D. Neither direct nor inverse proportion
questions.a: I-B, II-A, III-D, IV-C

questions.q:
On a farm, the water tank can be filled using one of two pairs of pumps. Pump A alone fills it in 6 hours and pump B alone in 9 hours. Pump C alone fills it in 5 hours and pump D alone in 20 hours.
(a) What part of the tank does each of pumps A and B fill in 1 hour?
(b) What part of the tank do A and B fill together in 1 hour?
(c) How long do A and B take to fill the tank together? Give the answer in hours and minutes.
(d) How long do C and D take to fill the tank together?
(e) The farmer needs the empty tank filled within 3 hours 45 minutes. Which pair should he run? Pump C is the fastest single pump; explain why its pair is still not the right choice.
questions.a: (a) Pump A fills 1/6 and pump B fills 1/9 of the tank in 1 hour. (b) 1/6 + 1/9 = 3/18 + 2/18 = 5/18 of the tank. (c) 18/5 = 3.6 hours = 3 hours 36 minutes. (d) 1/5 + 1/20 = 4/20 + 1/20 = 5/20 = 1/4 of the tank per hour, so they take 4 hours. (e) Pair A and B: 3 hours 36 minutes is within 3 hours 45 minutes, but C and D take 4 hours, which is too long. C is faster than A, but D is so slow (1/20 per hour) that the pair C and D fills less per hour (1/4) than A and B (5/18), so the pair's combined rate decides, not the fastest pump.
s: (a) Rates 1/6 and 1/9 of the tank per hour
(b) Combined rate 5/18 of the tank per hour
(e) Chooses A and B; compares combined rates 5/18 and 1/4

questions.q:
A scout camp in Pachmarhi has stored rations that will feed 60 scouts for 10 days. Every scout eats the same amount each day, and one ration packet feeds one scout for one day. Before the camp starts, the organisers learn that 15 more scouts are joining, making 75 in all, and the camp must still run for the full 10 days.
(a) How many ration packets are in the store?
(b) For how many days would the stored rations last for 75 scouts?
(c) How many packets do 75 scouts need for 10 days, and how many extra packets must be bought?
(d) One organiser suggests buying nothing and giving each scout only 4/5 of a packet a day. Would the store then last 10 days? Which plan would you choose for a camp with long hikes, and why?
questions.a: (a) 60 x 10 = 600 packets. (b) 60 x 10 = 75 x y, so y = 600 / 75 = 8 days. (c) 75 x 10 = 750 packets are needed, so 750 - 600 = 150 extra packets must be bought. (d) Daily use would be 75 x 4/5 = 60 packets, so 600 / 60 = 10 days: yes, it would last. But each scout would eat a fifth less every day; for a camp with long hikes, buying the 150 extra packets is the better choice because the scouts need their full ration, even though the cut saves money.
s: (d) Shows the cut ration lasts exactly 10 days and makes a reasoned choice
